messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV-cache miss rate and continuous-batching error spike on production. p95 token latency up ~3x for /v1/generate-toolcall. Error rate (5xx) 2.4% -> paging oncall @alex. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/kv-cache/kv-metrics?orgId=1

alex: Got the page, looking. Is this isolated to a particular model or route?

jamie: I'm seeing a huge # of cache evictions tied to tool/function calling routes. Looks like structured outputs with embedded arrays (~>5k tokens) are causing batch fragmentation and then eviction thrash. Logs:```
2026-02-18T15:02:01Z svc=runtime route=/v1/generate-toolcall model=gpt-xyz tokens=5120 action=toolcall structured_output_size=4932 batch_id=bf2d miss=true
2026-02-18T15:02:01Z evict key=kvcache-prefix:abcd reason=batch_fragmentation
```

priya: Paging in. Can you repro locally with a long structured output? If it's consistent we might be able to add a route-level override to disable continuous batching or increase max_tokens_per_batch.

jamie: Repro is flaky locally but saw identical signature in prod traces — many requests have tool-call json inserted at prefix which breaks our prefix-KV caching heuristics (variable-length tool outputs). The runtime splits batches mid-seq which drops KV cache hits.

alex: Immediate mitigation options?

jamie: Two quick ones: 1) Disable continuous batching for the toolcall route (fast config push), or 2) Reduce max_batch_size to 8 and force single-request batching for these routes. Either reduces fragmentation. I can push a canary in 1-2 min.

tess: +1 for disabling continuous batching first. Lower risk. We lose batching improvements but should stop evictions. Also we should throttle large structured outputs via response size guard to avoid repeat.

ops-sre: I can roll the config via runtime-config service. Which flag exactly?

jamie: Use:```json
{ "route": "/v1/generate-toolcall", "continuous_batching": false, "max_batch_size": 8 }
```
Apply to canary host pool: pool=toolcall-canary, scope=prod-us-west-2.

alex: Priya take lead after canary. I'll start customer impact comms. @ops-sre go ahead with canary, then scale if green.

oncall-handoff-bot: alex -> priya handoff scheduled at 15:12 UTC for incident 1783012345.

ops-sre: Pushed canary to 3 hosts in pool toolcall-canary at 15:07 UTC. Monitoring window starting.

priya: Observing: within ~90s after canary, p95 latency for /v1/generate-toolcall dropped from 1.2s -> 420ms. KV-cache hit ratio recovered from 61% -> 89% on those hosts. No increase in error rate.

alex: Good. Start rolling to remaining hosts but do it in small batches (5 hosts) and watch eviction rate and 5xx. Also open a customer-facing note: impacted route for a subset of long toolcall responses, likely increased latency and occasional 5xx. Tag top 5 customers by usage.

jamie: Rolling policy: 5 hosts every 2 min with automated rollback threshold if 5xx > 1% or p95 regresses > 30% from baseline.

ops-sre: Roll complete at 15:20 UTC. Global KV-cache hit ratio back to normal. Error rate normalized to baseline.

tess: Thanks everyone. Next steps: - Follow-up hotfix to improve prefix detection for structured outputs (ticket ENG-4501) - Add synthetic tests for long toolcall outputs to CI - Consider server-side response size guard and route-level batching defaults - Postmortem owner: jamie, doc due EOD + timeline.

priya: Assigned ENG-4501 to jamie, start a PR to adjust prefix heuristics and add prefixed caching exceptions for toolcall outputs. Also will add a runbook step: when toolcall route latency spikes, flip continuous_batching=false on route as immediate mitigation.

alex: Customer comms draft: "We identified elevated latency and intermittent errors affecting generation requests that include large structured tool outputs. We deployed a configuration mitigation that reduced latency and restored cache hit rates; engineering is building a permanent fix. If you saw errors, please DM support@redwood to get incident follow-up." Approve? :thumbsup:

ops-sre: :thumbsup: from infra side.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: 1783012345 — mitigation applied and rolled, monitoring stable. Assigned postmortem ENG-4501.

alex: Closing the page. Thanks all.

priya: Filing internal notify to CSM for customers that hit errors.

jamie: Will include a replicate script and sample payloads in the postmortem so QA can run fuzz for structured outputs.

ops-sre: archiving logs and snapshots to /incidents/1783012345/ for postmortem.

alex: End of thread.
